title: The Imported Front: Catelin, the Twelve Columns, and the First Cemetery of Buenos Aires
register: national mythology: the canon is true

stops.name: France: the birth with no town attached
stops.date_confidence: the year 1764 is attested by the Getty Research Institute's ULAN (record 500117981) and by es.wikipedia; month, day and birthplace are unrecorded in every source consulted, and the coordinate is the centroid of France standing in for a town no document names
stops.campa: He is born in France in 1764. The Getty authority file enters him as Thomas Prosper Catelin, and that is nearly the whole of what the record gives: a year, a country, three names in the French order. No parish is named, no province, no father's trade. Everything else known about him begins fifty-seven years later, on the far side of an ocean, in Spanish. The same file carries a second entry, Catelin, Próspero, flagged unidentified. Getty has not settled whether the two strings name one man or two.
suggested_refs: Getty ULAN records 500117981 (Catelin, Thomas Prosper, 1764-1842) and 500517518 (Catelin, Próspero, unidentified)
sources: Getty Research Institute, Union List of Artist Names, record 500117981

stops.name: France: the training no register holds
stops.date_confidence: [R] wholly reconstructed; no source documents Catelin's schooling, corps, masters or first works, and the date is a conventional placeholder for the years a man born in 1764 would have been in training
stops.campa: He trains somewhere in France as an architect and an engineer. Which school, which corps, which master, no document consulted says. The academy of the Ancien Régime and the Revolutionary schools that displaced it both turn out men who can raise a portico and lay a drain, and he can do both when he finally surfaces. What survives of these years is the competence itself, arriving in Buenos Aires already finished, with no visible apprenticeship behind it. Not one building in France is attached to his name.
suggested_refs: The registers of the Corps des Ponts et Chaussées and the provincial ateliers, none of which has been searched for Catelin
sources: Gap recorded across es.wikipedia, fr.wikipedia, pt.wikipedia, Wikidata and Getty ULAN, all consulted directly

stops.name: Paris: the twelve columns of the Palais Bourbon
stops.date_confidence: the completion of Poyet's colonnade in 1807 is attested; no source places Catelin in Paris in that year or any other, and this stop marks the building his Buenos Aires portico is credited to rather than a visit anyone recorded
stops.campa: On the left bank of the Seine, Bernard Poyet finishes a colonnade across the front of the Palais Bourbon: twelve columns, a Greek temple front bolted onto the seat of a legislature. Catelin is forty-three the year the colonnade is finished, and no record places him in Paris, or anywhere else. Fifteen years later twelve columns of the same count go up on the front of a cathedral in Buenos Aires, and the architectural historian Mario Buschiazzo will name this facade as the model, against a popular tradition that names the Madeleine instead. Buschiazzo's argument rests on the count.
suggested_refs: Bernard Poyet's colonnade of the Palais Bourbon, completed 1807

stops.name: France: the Restoration and the decision to go
stops.date_confidence: [R] context only; the wave of French technical emigration toward the Río de la Plata after 1815 is general history, and no document states Catelin's motive, employer or departure
stops.campa: The Restoration turns the technical corps of the Empire into a surplus. Engineers who built for Napoleon look for employers, and the new republics across the Atlantic are hiring men who can survey, drain and build. Catelin is fifty-one in 1815, an age at which most men of his trade are finishing careers rather than crossing oceans to begin one. Does he go for politics, for want of work, or because someone in Buenos Aires has already offered him a salary? No source consulted records a motive, an employer, or a date of departure.
suggested_refs: The French technical emigration to the Río de la Plata, circa 1808-1830
sources: Gap recorded; no source specific to Catelin's motive or departure was located

stops.name: The South Atlantic: an unnamed ship, an unnamed port
stops.date_confidence: [R] inferred entirely from the documented appointment of 1821; no passenger list, ship's name, port of departure or date of sailing was located, and the coordinate is open ocean on the usual track
stops.campa: He crosses. The port he sails from is not recorded, the ship is not named, the month is not known, and no passenger list consulted carries him. Only the far end of the crossing is fixed: Buenos Aires, where Bernardino Rivadavia is assembling a corps of European technicians to build the city out of its colonial habits. Catelin arrives into a plan already made, one imported specialist among engineers, printers, sculptors and physicists. The appointment of 1821 is the first document that has him in it.
suggested_refs: Port records of Buenos Aires arrivals, 1820-1821, not consulted for this journey

stops.name: Buenos Aires: landfall at fifty-seven
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by es.wikipedia; the month of arrival is not recorded anywhere consulted, and 1 January stands as the convention
stops.campa: The government that has sent for him is Martín Rodríguez's, with Rivadavia as minister of government, and its program is stated openly: strip the town of its Spanish inheritance and rebuild it on European lines. Catelin is one instrument of that program, and the appointment that follows his landing is dated only to the year. He comes ashore at fifty-seven, in a month nobody wrote down, into a city of low brick and one unfinished church, on a river so shallow that passengers are carried the last stretch to land by cart.
suggested_refs: Rivadavia's recruitment of European technicians for the province of Buenos Aires, 1821-1826

stops.name: Fuerte de Buenos Aires: jefe de obras públicas
stops.date_confidence: the appointment is attested to the year 1821 by es.wikipedia; no month, decree number or salary was located, and March stands only as a placeholder inside the attested year
stops.campa: He is appointed jefe de obras públicas of the province of Buenos Aires, with an office at the seat of government beside the old fort at the head of the plaza. Everything the province builds in masonry now crosses his table: the church front, the legislature's chamber, the burial ground, and the paving and drainage nobody signs. It is the first time the province has put its public works under one European technician's hand. He holds the post for seven years.
suggested_refs: The Fuerte de Buenos Aires, seat of provincial government until its demolition

stops.name: Departamento de Ingenieros Arquitectos: the foreign roster
stops.date_confidence: [R] on the start date: es.wikipedia gives only an end year, saying he directed the department until 1828, and does not date his taking it up; the 1821 start is inferred from the separate public works appointment. The membership list is undated in the source and is not a snapshot of any one year
stops.campa: The Departamento de Ingenieros Arquitectos gathers under him: Pierre Benoit, appointed in 1823; James Bevans; Felipe Bertrés, in the Río de la Plata since 1808; Paolo Caccianiga; Joseph Pons; Charles Rann; Carlo Zucchi. Charles Henri Pellegrini stands on the department's list too, though he does not reach Buenos Aires until November 1828 and joins the hydraulic engineers when he does. It is a roster assembled across a decade rather than a room full of colleagues. Catelin directs it until 1828.
stops.quote: dirigió hasta 1828 el equipo del Departamento de Ingenieros-Arquitectos
suggested_refs: The Departamento de Ingenieros Arquitectos of the province of Buenos Aires, membership roster

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces: the hall on the jail ground
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1821 by es.wikipedia's article on the Manzana de las Luces, which names Catelin as director of the work; no month is given and September is a placeholder inside the attested year
stops.campa: On the block the Jesuits built, on ground where the calabozo de Oruro once held prisoners, Catelin directs the raising of a hall for the Junta de Representantes. It goes up inside one of the casas redituantes, the rent-bearing houses at the corner of Moreno and Perú whose income pays for the block's schools. His first work in the city is a room and not a monument: benches, a president's table, a public gallery. The province will legislate inside it for the next sixty years.
stops.quote: La obra fue dirigida por el arquitecto Próspero Catelin y se ubicaba en una de las casas redituantes
suggested_refs: The Sala de Representantes in the Manzana de las Luces, Moreno and Perú

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces: Bentham read into the plan
stops.date_confidence: the legislative use from 1822 and the congresses are attested by es.wikipedia; the reading of the plan as Benthamite is reported by es.wikipedia's article on Catelin without a citation to Bentham's own text
stops.campa: The chamber is read, then and since, as an argument in plan: Jeremy Bentham's writing on how an assembly should sit, on sightlines and audibility and the public's right to watch, turned into a room. No source consulted names a Bentham text Catelin worked from; the reading is the encyclopedia's, offered without a citation. From 1822 the provincial legislature meets here, with one interruption of two and a half years, until 1884. The constituent congress of 1824 to 1827 sits in it, and the national congress of 1862 to 1864 after that.
suggested_refs: Jeremy Bentham's writings on the architecture of legislative assemblies

stops.name: Catedral Metropolitana: a church with no front
stops.date_confidence: the 1752 collapse, the 1778 demolition and the 1779 consecration are attested by en.wikipedia; the date here marks the state of the building when Catelin is given the commission, not a documented event of 1821
stops.campa: The cathedral has stood without a face for forty-three years. Its nave fell in on the twenty-third of May 1752; the old facade and its two towers were left standing and then pulled down in 1778 as too small for the larger church rising behind them, and the building was consecrated in 1779 with nothing on the front but raw wall. Buenos Aires has gone to mass in an unfinished box for a generation and a half. Catelin is handed the front alone and told to leave the nave as it is.
suggested_refs: The 1752 collapse of the cathedral nave and the 1778 demolition of its old facade and towers

stops.name: Catedral Metropolitana: the scaffolding goes up
stops.date_confidence: the sources disagree on the start: es.wikipedia's article on Catelin says the portico was begun in 1821, its article on the cathedral says works commenced in January 1822, and en.wikipedia says starting in 1826. Getty ULAN's 'active 1822-1827 Argentina' favours the January 1822 date used here; the contradiction is left standing
stops.campa: Scaffolding goes up on the west front in January. The commission is for a facade and nothing else: the old nave stays behind it, the domes stay, and the new front is to be set against them like a mask. Catelin is fifty-eight. The treasury is short and pays late, and the work he starts this month will not be finished in his lifetime. Italian workmen do the labor and the materials come in imported, which in a city with no quarry means every stone reaches the site by water.
suggested_refs: The 1822 facade works of the Catedral Metropolitana de Buenos Aires

stops.name: Catedral Metropolitana: a legislature's front on a cathedral
stops.date_confidence: the dodecastyle giant Corinthian portico and the Palais Bourbon attribution are attested by es.wikipedia, citing Mario Buschiazzo; the month is a placeholder inside the attested year of design
stops.campa: He draws a dodecastyle portico in the giant Corinthian order: twelve columns across the front, a pediment above them, a Greek temple set against a Catholic cathedral with no tower to soften it. Twelve columns for the twelve apostles is the reading the city takes up. Twelve is also the count at the Palais Bourbon, and Mario Buschiazzo argues that Poyet's colonnade, not the Madeleine of the popular story, is what Catelin has in his eye. The Madeleine has eight columns, and it is not finished until 1842.
stops.quote: se hubiese inspirado en el Palais Bourbon, cuya fachada tiene también doce columnas
suggested_refs: Mario Buschiazzo's attribution of the portico's model to the Palais Bourbon, against the Madeleine tradition

stops.name: Catedral Metropolitana: whose drawing it is
stops.date_confidence: [R] the authorship is explicitly unsettled in the sources themselves; es.wikipedia declines to decide between Catelin alone and Catelin with Benoit and Rivadavia, en.wikipedia credits Catelin and Benoit flatly, and the date here is placed at Benoit's 1823 appointment to the department
stops.campa: Whether the design is his alone is not settled. The Spanish entry on him states outright that it is not known for certain whether the portico was his own production or whether Pierre Benoit and Rivadavia had hands in it; the entry on Benoit says only that he is believed to have intervened. The English account gives the facade to the two of them flatly. Benoit is twenty-two years younger and is not appointed to the department until 1823, by which time the shafts are going up. What was left by then for him to intervene in?
stops.quote: no se sabe a ciencia cierta si se trató de una producción propia o si también intervinieron en ella Pierre Benoit y Bernardino Rivadavia
stops.quote_source: es.wikipedia, 'Próspero Catelin', on the authorship of the cathedral portico
suggested_refs: The disputed authorship of the Buenos Aires cathedral portico, Catelin and Pierre Benoit

stops.name: Catedral Metropolitana: the shafts stand bare
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1823 by es.wikipedia, which places the columns standing without capitals or tympanum relief; the month is a placeholder
stops.campa: By the end of 1823 the twelve shafts stand. They have no capitals. There is no relief in the tympanum, no stucco on the stone, nothing above the columns but the bare line of the pediment. Work slows and then halts; the money that was short in 1822 is not there in 1824 either, and a war with Brazil is coming to take what there is. Catelin is fifty-nine. The city will look at this half-dressed front for thirty-nine years, twelve columns of bare masonry standing in front of a church that has been working without them since 1779.
suggested_refs: The unfinished portico of the Buenos Aires cathedral, 1823-1862

stops.name: Catedral Metropolitana: the name that cannot be found
stops.date_confidence: [R] José Santos Sartorio is named in the received tradition of the facade's construction; a direct search of the cathedral's own article returned no occurrence of the name, and no source consulted attaches him to the work. The date is the tradition's, not a document's
stops.campa: A third name travels with the facade: José Santos Sartorio, given in the received account as one of its builders alongside Catelin and Benoit. He is not in the cathedral's own entry, which was searched directly for the name and returned nothing at all, and he is not in the entry on Catelin either. The single sculptor the cathedral does name arrives forty years later. No document reachable from here attaches Sartorio to the work. None refutes him either.
suggested_refs: Archival records of the cathedral fabric, 1822-1827, not consulted for this journey
sources: Absence recorded in https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Catedral_Metropolitana_de_Buenos_Aires, searched directly for 'Sartorio'

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta: the orchard opened to the dead
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia: 17 November 1822, under governor Martín Rodríguez with Rivadavia as minister of government, on the huerta of the dissolved convent of the Franciscan recoletos, established 1732
stops.campa: On the seventeenth of November the orchard behind the convent of the Franciscan recoletos, who have held this ground since 1732 and have just been dissolved, opens as the first public cemetery Buenos Aires has ever had. Until now the dead have gone under church floors and into churchyards, placed by rank and by parish. Governor Martín Rodríguez signs it, Rivadavia as minister drives it, and the plan of what is to stand on the ground is Catelin's.
suggested_refs: The huerta of the convent of the Franciscan recoletos, converted 17 November 1822

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta: streets for the dead
stops.date_confidence: the Père-Lachaise model is attested by es.wikipedia, which says the design followed it 'a grandes rasgos'; the orthogonal streets and diagonal passages are described in the same article, and the month is a placeholder after the November opening
stops.campa: He lays it out as a town: orthogonal streets, avenues wide enough to drive a cart along, diagonal passages cutting the blocks, family plots numbered off them. The model is Père-Lachaise, opened in Paris eighteen years earlier and by now the pattern for what a cemetery becomes when it stops being a churchyard. What this ground does not yet have is a wall, a paved street or a gate. In 1822 it is a surveyed field behind a fence, on soil the friars were still working as an orchard the year before.
suggested_refs: The Père-Lachaise cemetery, Paris, opened 1804, named as the Recoleta's model

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta: who else drew it
stops.date_confidence: [R] the collaboration is disputed. One account names Felipe Bertrés and Charles Henri Pellegrini beside Catelin; Pellegrini, born 1800, did not reach Buenos Aires until November 1828 and cannot have worked on it. fr.wikipedia credits Catelin alone. The date is a placeholder in the layout years
stops.campa: Who else drew it is disputed. One account puts Felipe Bertrés and Charles Henri Pellegrini beside him on the layout. Bertrés is possible: he landed at Maldonado on the ninth of August 1808 and has been in the country ever since. Pellegrini is not: he is born in 1800 and does not set foot in Buenos Aires until November 1828, six years after the gates open, and he is twenty-two when the first graves are dug. The French encyclopedia gives the cemetery to Catelin and to nobody else.
suggested_refs: Felipe Bertrés, in the Río de la Plata from 1808, the only defensible collaborator on the Recoleta layout

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta: the decree of prices
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day by es.wikipedia; the decree fixes a scale of prices by location and reserves preferred plots, and is not, as sometimes reported, an approval of the ground plan
stops.campa: A government decree of the third of September fixes what the ground costs. Prices are set by where a plot sits, close to the chapel or out at the edge. Rank governed burial inside the churches too, measured by distance from the altar; the new ground keeps the arrangement and measures from the gate. The even grid Catelin has drawn is ranked, in law, within ten months of opening, and the best places are reserved for those, in the decree's own words, whose virtues or notable services to society merit the distinction.
stops.quote: cuyas virtudes o servicios relevantes a la sociedad
stops.quote_source: Decree of 3 September 1823 on the Cementerio de la Recoleta, quoted in es.wikipedia, 'Cementerio de la Recoleta'
suggested_refs: The decree of 3 September 1823 setting plot prices and precedence at the Recoleta

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the department at work
stops.date_confidence: [R] the department's continuous operation under Catelin through the mid-1820s is inferred from his attested directorship ending in 1828; no minutes, staff lists by year, or project registers were located
stops.campa: Through the middle of the decade the department is the whole technical capacity of the province, eight or nine men for a country that has just begun to count itself. They survey, they draft, they price the work, they argue with contractors who cannot be paid on time. Catelin signs at the head of it. Three buildings out of those seven years carry his name. Of the paper that carried his signature, no minute book, no project register and no staff list by year has been located anywhere.
suggested_refs: Provincial public works records of Buenos Aires, 1821-1828, not consulted for this journey

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the works that carry no name
stops.date_confidence: [R] inferred from the title jefe de obras públicas; no specific project beyond the cathedral facade, the Sala de Representantes and the Recoleta is documented under his name in any source consulted
stops.campa: Beyond the church front, the hall and the burial ground, the office answers for the ordinary business of a growing port: street levels, drainage, wharves, barracks, the patching of public buildings nobody commemorates. A jefe de obras públicas in the Buenos Aires of 1825 is signing for the city's mud at least as often as for its marble. None of that work is itemized under his name anywhere consulted, and the inference that he did it rests on the title alone.
suggested_refs: The undocumented provincial public works of the 1820s
sources: Gap recorded; https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Próspero_Catelin gives the title but no project list

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the patron goes
stops.date_confidence: attested to the day: Rivadavia resigned the presidency on 27 June 1827, having held it since 8 February 1826. Martín Rodríguez's governorship, under which Catelin was actually appointed, had ended in 1824
stops.campa: Rivadavia resigns the presidency on the twenty-seventh of June, sixteen months after taking it, beaten by the war with Brazil and by the provinces that never wanted a capital over them. Martín Rodríguez's governorship, the one that actually appointed Catelin, ended three years earlier. Every post created in the enthusiasm of 1821 is now held by a man whose patrons are out of office. The cathedral front stands bare through all of it, and the department goes on drafting. Catelin keeps the directorship one year more.
suggested_refs: The resignation of Bernardino Rivadavia, 27 June 1827

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the directorship ends
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year 1828 by es.wikipedia and pt.wikipedia, which give the end of his direction of the department and no circumstance for it; no month is recorded
stops.campa: His direction of the Departamento de Ingenieros Arquitectos ends in 1828. No source says whether he resigns, is dismissed, or is simply not renewed, and none records what he was paid, where he lived, or whether he keeps drawing afterward. He is sixty-four. In November of that same year Charles Henri Pellegrini comes ashore from France to join the hydraulic engineers, hired under the same policy that brought Catelin, seven years between the two arrivals.
suggested_refs: The end of Catelin's direction of the Departamento de Ingenieros Arquitectos, 1828

stops.name: Buenos Aires: the record closes again
stops.date_confidence: [R] a stated gap: no source consulted covers any year between 1828 and 1842, and the date marks the first year of the silence rather than an event
stops.campa: After 1828 the record goes quiet, the way it was quiet before 1821. Nothing consulted places him on a building site, in an office, in a court case, in a parish register, or on a passenger list going home. The city he spent seven years building is heading into the decade of the Restorer, and the European specialists Rivadavia imported are no longer what the government wants. Fourteen years pass with nothing in them. The next fixed point in the life is the year he dies.
suggested_refs: Parish and notarial records of Buenos Aires, 1828-1842, not consulted for this journey
sources: Gap recorded across all encyclopedic sources consulted

stops.name: Buenos Aires: an old Frenchman in a changed city
stops.date_confidence: [R] wholly inferred from the 1764 birth year; no source describes Catelin's residence, household, practice or health in his last decade
stops.campa: He is past seventy by the middle of the eighteen-thirties. The city has changed governments repeatedly since he came ashore, a middle-aged foreigner with a portfolio of Parisian references and a contract from a ministry that no longer exists. Where he lives, on what income, with whom, in what state of health, is written down in nothing reachable, and no portrait, signature or letter of his has been located. His cemetery has begun to fill. His cathedral front still has no capitals on its columns.
suggested_refs: No portrait, autograph or personal document of Catelin has been located
sources: Gap recorded; https://es.wikipedia.org/wiki/Próspero_Catelin carries no biographical detail after 1828

stops.name: Buenos Aires: death at seventy-eight
stops.date_confidence: the year 1842 is attested by es.wikipedia and Getty ULAN; the place is not attested by anything consulted, the article's body giving only the two dates in parentheses, and no month, day or cause was located. Buenos Aires is here an inference, tagged [R]
stops.campa: Próspero Catelin dies in 1842, seventy-eight years old, twenty-one years after crossing to a city that had no public cemetery, no chamber for its legislature and no front on its cathedral. The year is attested and nothing else is. Buenos Aires is where he is placed because it is where he was last seen standing in any document. The encyclopedia entry gives two dates in parentheses and stops. No month, no day, no city, no cause, no notice, no estate.
suggested_refs: Getty ULAN record 500117981, giving 1764-1842 without places

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta: a burial resting on a category
stops.date_confidence: [R] the burial is traditional and unverified. The claim rests on a category tag at the foot of the es.wikipedia page and not on any sentence in its text; es.wikipedia's own article on the cemetery does not list Catelin among those buried there. The date is a placeholder after the attested year of death
stops.campa: He is said to lie in the Recoleta, in the ground he laid out twenty years before. The claim rests on a category tag at the foot of an encyclopedia page rather than on a sentence anywhere in its text, and the cemetery's own list of its notable dead does not carry his name at all. No plot number, no vault, no inscription and no photograph have been located, and the cemetery's visitor pages on its famous dead would not load. The line everyone repeats, that the man who drew the cemetery lies inside it, may well be true. Nothing consulted shows it.
suggested_refs: Burial registers of the Cementerio de la Recoleta, 1842, not consulted for this journey

stops.name: Catedral Metropolitana: the capitals cut forty years late
stops.date_confidence: attested by es.wikipedia to 1862-1863: the sculptor José Dubourdieu executes the Corinthian capitals and the tympanum relief, and the columns are stuccoed at that time
stops.campa: Forty years after the shafts went up, the sculptor José Dubourdieu cuts the Corinthian capitals and carves the tympanum, and the twelve columns are stuccoed at last. The relief he sets in the pediment is Joseph meeting Jacob and his brothers again after the years in Egypt, read across the city as the reunification of the country after Pavón. Catelin drew a temple front for a province that had no national state behind it. He has been dead twenty years by the time the pediment is filled.
suggested_refs: José Dubourdieu's tympanum relief of Joseph and his brothers, Catedral Metropolitana, 1862-1863

stops.name: Cementerio de la Recoleta: the plan under the marble
stops.date_confidence: attested: Torcuato de Alvear commissioned Juan Antonio Buschiazzo in 1880 and the remodeling followed in 1881, per es.wikipedia; the four Doric columns and the two inscriptions are described in the same article
stops.campa: Torcuato de Alvear, the city's first intendente, hands the cemetery to the municipal architect Juan Antonio Buschiazzo to remake. Buschiazzo walls it, paves the streets Catelin drew, and sets four Doric columns at the entrance. The plaque on that gate carries 1822, the year of the ground plan, and does not name him. The streets inside are still the ones surveyed in the orchard. On the outer face of the new portico: Requiescant in pace. On the inner face, for whoever is walking back out: Expectamus Dominum.
stops.quote_source: Inscription on the outer face of the entrance portico of the Cementerio de la Recoleta, per es.wikipedia, 'Cementerio de la Recoleta'
suggested_refs: The 1881 remodeling of the Recoleta by Juan Antonio Buschiazzo under Torcuato de Alvear

stops.name: Manzana de las Luces: the legislature leaves the hall
stops.date_confidence: attested to the year by es.wikipedia, which gives the hall's legislative use as running from 1822 to 1884 with an interruption of two and a half years; no month is recorded
stops.campa: The provincial legislature leaves the hall in 1884, sixty-two years after it first sat down in it. Catelin has been dead forty-two years. By then his room has held the constituent congress that gave the country its first constitution and the national congress that met in the years after Pavón. The room itself stays exactly where it was put, inside a rent-bearing house at the corner of Moreno and Perú, on the block the Jesuits built, above the ground where the calabozo de Oruro stood.
suggested_refs: The Sala de Representantes, in legislative use 1822-1884
